steps.say: Many things use electricity. Some plug into the wall and some use batteries.

figure.alt: A lamp bulb and a battery.

steps.say: Mains electricity comes from wall sockets. It is very strong.
Batteries store a small amount of electricity. Torches and remotes use them.
Keep water away from electricity. Never poke anything into a socket.
Fly kites far from power lines. Tell an adult about fallen wires.

figure.alt: A kite and a power line.

steps.say: A bulb lights up when a battery and wires make a complete loop.

figure.alt: A battery and a lit bulb joined in a complete loop.

options.text: touching a switch with wet hands
options.why: Water and electricity are a dangerous mix.

options.text: asking an adult to plug in a lamp
pushing a pencil into a socket
options.why: Never put anything into a socket.

hints: Think about water, sockets and poles.
Ask: which one keeps you away from danger?
check.explanation: Asking an adult to plug in a lamp is safe. The others could give a dangerous shock.

options.why: A fridge plugs into the wall.
A washing machine plugs into the wall.
An electric kettle plugs into the wall.

hints: Things we carry around often use batteries.
Think about what you hold to change the TV channel.
check.explanation: A TV remote uses small batteries. The others plug into the wall.
